standard_prerequisites.name: Direct sums described by four morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the list of identities satisfied by the two injections and the two projections of a direct sum, which is the data transported by the functor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterizations of the zero object
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the characterization of the zero object by which the second assertion is proved.

core_obligations: Direct sums (proof lines 396-404): once a direct sum z of x and y is described as an object with four morphisms satisfying the identities listed in the citation, additivity of the functor shows that F(z) together with F(i), F(j), F(p) and F(q) satisfies exactly the same identities, so F(z) is a direct sum of F(x) and F(y).
Zero objects (proof lines 406-412): the functor carries zero objects to zero objects by the cited characterization.
proof_roadmap: Recall the identities characterising a direct sum by four morphisms.
Transport those identities through the additive functor.
Apply a characterization of the zero object for the second assertion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an additive functor between preadditive categories carries direct sums to direct sums and zero objects to zero objects (statement lines 389-394). The proof is a complete argument: a direct sum is characterised by four morphisms satisfying a short list of identities, and since the functor is additive it carries each identity to the corresponding identity between the images of those morphisms, which makes the image of the direct sum a direct sum of the images (proof lines 396-404); the statement about zero objects is then read off from a characterization of the zero object (proof lines 406-412). The non-formal content is the transport of the identities. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
